title: Dairy-Free Lemon Blossom Cupcakes
shortDescription: Bright lemon cupcakes with 25 minutes of prep and 18 minutes of baking, topped with a light dairy-free lemon cream frosting.
description: These cupcakes taste like fresh lemon zest in every bite. I tested this batch in my own kitchen using dairy-free butter and oat milk, and the crumb still came out soft and moist. The frosting is simple: dairy-free butter, powdered sugar, and lots of lemon juice. No cream cheese or heavy cream needed, so it stays light and holds its swirl. Zest does the real work here. I use both lemon zest and juice, which gives a brighter lemon taste than juice alone. This recipe is a good pick for spring parties or anyone who needs a dairy-free treat that does not feel like a substitute.
instructions: Heat your oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat the dairy-free butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Mix in the dairy-free milk, lemon juice, lemon zest, and vanilla extract.
Add the flour mix in two batches, stirring just until no dry streaks remain.
Divide the batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool the cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move them to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat the dairy-free butter for the frosting until smooth, about 1 minute.
Add powdered sugar, lemon juice, lemon zest, and salt. Beat until light and fluffy.
Pipe the frosting onto the cooled cupcakes and top with extra lemon zest if you like.
tips: Zest your lemons before you juice them. It is much easier that way.
Chill the frosting for 10 minutes if it feels too soft to pipe tall swirls.
Use room temperature eggs so the batter mixes evenly and rises well.
Store leftovers in the fridge since the frosting has no dairy fat to stabilize it at room temperature.

faq.question: Can I use bottled lemon juice instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Fresh juice tastes brighter and pairs better with the zest. Bottled juice works in a pinch but the lemon flavor will be milder.

faq.question: What dairy-free milk works best in this recipe?
faq.answer: I tested this with both almond milk and oat milk, and both worked well. Oat milk gives a slightly richer crumb.

faq.question: Why is my dairy-free frosting too soft to pipe?
faq.answer: Some dairy-free butters are softer than dairy butter. Chill the frosting for 10 to 15 minutes before piping.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to a day ahead and store them unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost them the day you plan to serve.

conclusion: These lemon blossom cupcakes prove dairy-free baking can still taste bright and rich. The lemon frosting is easy to make and holds a tall swirl without any dairy at all.
